_note: Curated, hand-verified POIs across NV/CA/AZ/UT. Coordinates are real (lat,lon). 'kind' is the headline type; 'services' is what you can do there (gas/lodging/food). Encounters carry language+voice for Kokoro NPCs. Arbitrary street addresses are resolved live via OSM geocoding; this set seeds the authored map and the survival lattice.

start.name: SEMA — LVCC North Hall
start.blurb: The show floor at twenty minutes to close. Compressors, a rev-limiter slapping the rafters, ten thousand people who all think they know cars. She's on the turntable, white under the lights — and the placard doesn't mention she talks.

pois.name: Paradise Road Chevron, behind the LVCC North Hall
pois.blurb: Neon on wet asphalt. The show is still roaring two blocks back. The pump island is empty and the needle is near E.

pois.name: Las Vegas
pois.blurb: The Strip, the convention halls, ten thousand cameras. A bright place to be a car nobody can quite account for.

pois.name: Las Vegas Motor Speedway
pois.blurb: A 1.5-mile tri-oval and a dragstrip out in the desert north of town.

pois.name: Spring Mountain Motorsports Ranch, Pahrump
pois.blurb: Members' road course out past the Spring Mountains. Close enough to taste, far enough to strand you on a bad tank.

pois.name: Pahrump
pois.blurb: Casinos, a winery, and the last cheap gas before the Death Valley road.

pois.name: Valley of Fire State Park
pois.blurb: Aztec sandstone the color of a struck match. No fuel out here. Plan it.

pois.name: Mesquite
pois.blurb: Last Nevada town on I-15 before the Arizona slot and the Utah line. Fill here for Zion.

pois.name: Glendale / Moapa
pois.blurb: An off-ramp, a truck stop, a reservation smoke shop. Fuel on the I-15 run.

pois.name: Beatty
pois.blurb: Gateway to Death Valley from the north. Wild burros on the road at dusk.

pois.name: Primm
pois.blurb: A border casino with a roller coaster, straddling the California line on I-15.

pois.name: Laughlin
pois.blurb: Riverboat casinos on the Colorado, cheaper than Vegas, hot as a griddle.

pois.name: Hoover Dam / Boulder City
pois.blurb: 726 feet of Depression-era concrete holding back Lake Mead. Last gas in Boulder City.

pois.name: Tonopah
pois.blurb: Old silver town, the darkest skies in the lower 48, halfway up the middle of nowhere.

pois.name: Rachel / Extraterrestrial Highway
pois.blurb: The Little A'Le'Inn and 98 miles of empty SR-375. Top off before you commit; there is nothing out here.

pois.name: Ely
pois.blurb: A railroad town on the Loneliest Road, last stop before Great Basin.

pois.name: Great Basin National Park
pois.blurb: Wheeler Peak, bristlecone pines older than writing, the Lehman Caves. Almost nobody comes.

pois.name: Reno
pois.blurb: The Biggest Little City, up against the Sierra. A long way from the show.

pois.name: Carson City
pois.blurb: The quiet capital under the eastern slope of the Sierra.

pois.name: Baker
pois.blurb: The world's tallest thermometer and a Greek diner. Gateway to Death Valley from I-15.

pois.name: Barstow
pois.blurb: Where the desert highways knot together. Route 66 murals, a rail yard, cheap motels.

pois.name: Calico Ghost Town
pois.blurb: A silver boomtown that died and got bought by Knott's. Plank sidewalks above Barstow.

pois.name: Needles
pois.blurb: Where I-40 crosses the Colorado into California. Brutally hot, friendly enough.

pois.name: Death Valley NP (Furnace Creek)
pois.blurb: 282 feet below sea level, the hottest place on Earth. Gas here costs what they want it to.

pois.name: Stovepipe Wells
pois.blurb: A dune, a saloon, and a pump in the middle of Death Valley.

pois.name: Mojave
pois.blurb: Wind turbines, a spaceport, and rows of mothballed airliners in the dry air.

pois.name: Willow Springs International Raceway
pois.blurb: 'The Fastest Road in the West.' Nine turns of old California tarmac near Rosamond.

pois.name: Buttonwillow Raceway Park
pois.blurb: Flat, technical club track in the cotton fields west of Bakersfield.

pois.name: Auto Club Speedway (Fontana)
pois.blurb: A two-mile D-oval in the Inland Empire smog, on borrowed time.

pois.name: Chuckwalla Valley Raceway
pois.blurb: Desert road course out by Desert Center. Bring your own everything.

pois.name: WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca
pois.blurb: The Corkscrew. Eleven turns dropping through the Monterey hills like a dare.

pois.name: Thunderhill Raceway Park
pois.blurb: Five miles of track in the rice country near Willows, home of the 25-hour race.

pois.name: Sonoma Raceway
pois.blurb: Wine-country hills folded into a road course at the top of the bay.

pois.name: Joshua Tree National Park
pois.blurb: Where the Mojave meets the Colorado desert and the trees throw their arms up. No gas inside.

pois.name: Yosemite National Park
pois.blurb: El Capitan, Half Dome, the granite cathedral. Tioga Pass closes with the snow.

pois.name: Sequoia National Park
pois.blurb: The biggest living things that have ever stood. The road up is all switchbacks.

pois.name: Kings Canyon National Park
pois.blurb: A glacial gorge deeper than the Grand Canyon, and far emptier.

pois.name: Disneyland (Anaheim)
pois.blurb: The original. A monorail, a Matterhorn, and a parking structure the size of a town.

pois.name: Knott's Berry Farm (Buena Park)
pois.blurb: The boysenberry kingdom. Wooden coasters and a ghost town that owns Calico.

pois.name: Six Flags Magic Mountain (Valencia)
pois.blurb: Nineteen coasters stacked on a hill above the 5. The thrill-ride capital of the world.

pois.name: Universal Studios Hollywood
pois.blurb: A working backlot you can ride through, perched above the 101.

pois.name: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
pois.blurb: The Giant Dipper, salt air, and 1907 still running on the sand.

pois.name: SeaWorld San Diego
pois.blurb: Mission Bay, coasters, and the smell of the cold Pacific.

pois.name: Santa Monica Pier
pois.blurb: The Pacific Wheel and the end of Route 66, where the road runs out of country.

pois.name: Los Angeles
pois.blurb: Twelve million people and a freeway for every one of them.

pois.name: Little Tokyo, Los Angeles
pois.blurb: Lanterns over First Street, a mochi shop, a woman who does not switch to English when you stumble.
pois.npc: the okamisan at a Little Tokyo counter

pois.name: East Los Angeles
pois.blurb: Mariachi Plaza, taquerias, a mechanic who talks to your engine before he talks to you.

pois.name: Artesia / Little India
pois.blurb: Pioneer Boulevard: sari shops, sweets, and a chai cart that runs on its own time.
pois.npc: the chai-cart auntie on Pioneer Blvd

pois.name: San Diego
pois.blurb: Navy gray and surf gold, the last big city before the line.

pois.name: San Francisco
pois.blurb: Forty-three hills and the fog coming in over them. Park facing the curb or lose your tires.

pois.name: Japantown, San Francisco
pois.blurb: The Peace Pagoda, a bookstore, a ramen line. If you drove all this way, this is who you came to hear.
pois.npc: a shopkeeper in the Japan Center

pois.name: Chinatown, San Francisco
pois.blurb: The oldest Chinatown in the country. Grant Avenue, a tea seller who measures you with her eyes.
pois.npc: a tea seller on Grant Avenue

pois.name: North Beach, San Francisco
pois.blurb: Espresso, City Lights bookstore, an old man who calls every car bella.
pois.npc: a cafe owner on Columbus Avenue

pois.name: The Mission, San Francisco
pois.blurb: Murals down every alley and the best taqueria argument in the state.

pois.name: Bakersfield
pois.blurb: Oil derricks, the Bakersfield Sound, and the bottom of the Central Valley.

pois.name: Fresno
pois.blurb: The gateway to three national parks, flat and patient in the haze.

pois.name: Bishop
pois.blurb: The Eastern Sierra hub. Erick Schat's bakery, the High Sierra throwing shadows by four.

pois.name: Lone Pine
pois.blurb: Under Mt. Whitney, where a thousand Westerns were shot in the Alabama Hills.

pois.name: Lee Vining / Tioga Pass
pois.blurb: Mono Lake's tufa towers and the eastern gate to Yosemite, 9,943 feet up when it's open.

pois.name: Palm Springs
pois.blurb: Mid-century glass under the San Jacintos, a tram to the snow line above the heat.

pois.name: Grand Canyon NP (South Rim)
pois.blurb: A mile straight down and ten miles across. Gas and rooms at the village, if you booked.

pois.name: Grand Canyon NP (North Rim)
pois.blurb: A thousand feet higher, far emptier, closed once the snow comes.

pois.name: Flagstaff
pois.blurb: Ponderosa pines at 7,000 feet, Route 66 and the railroad, snow on the peaks.

pois.name: Williams
pois.blurb: The last town on Route 66 to be bypassed, and the rail gateway to the Grand Canyon.

pois.name: Kingman
pois.blurb: Heart of Route 66 Arizona, a crossroads of I-40 and the road up from Vegas.

pois.name: Lake Havasu City
pois.blurb: Someone bought the actual London Bridge and shipped it here, stone by stone.

pois.name: Sedona
pois.blurb: Red-rock spires, art galleries, and people who will tell you about the vortexes.

pois.name: Page / Horseshoe Bend
pois.blurb: Antelope Canyon's light shafts, the green river bending 270 degrees under your boots.

pois.name: Phoenix
pois.blurb: The Valley of the Sun, a grid of warm light spreading to every horizon.

pois.name: Castles N' Coasters (Phoenix)
pois.blurb: Arizona's last big amusement park: four mini-golf courses and the Desert Storm coaster.

pois.name: Tucson
pois.blurb: Saguaro forests, the old Spanish presidio, the Sonoran desert in bloom after rain.

pois.name: Nogales
pois.blurb: The border. The fence runs right through town and the language doesn't stop at it.
pois.npc: a vendor at the line in Nogales

pois.name: Saguaro National Park
pois.blurb: A forest of giant cactus standing watch over Tucson, arms raised against the dusk.

pois.name: Petrified Forest National Park
pois.blurb: Stone logs of a vanished jungle and the banded Painted Desert. No services, long miles.

pois.name: Monument Valley
pois.blurb: The mittens and the buttes on the Navajo line, the most filmed horizon in America.

pois.name: Meteor Crater
pois.blurb: A 50,000-year-old hole in the desert, three-quarters of a mile across, off old 66.

pois.name: St. George
pois.blurb: The first Utah town off I-15, red rock and a tabernacle. Fill here for Zion or Bryce.

pois.name: Springdale (Zion gate)
pois.blurb: The little town at the mouth of Zion Canyon. Shuttle, lodges, the cliffs leaning in overhead.

pois.name: Zion National Park
pois.blurb: Navajo sandstone walls 2,000 feet high, the Narrows, Angels Landing. The trip everyone tries to make on a splash of gas.

pois.name: Cedar City
pois.blurb: Festival town below the high plateaus, the turnoff for Bryce and Cedar Breaks.

pois.name: Kanab
pois.blurb: 'Little Hollywood,' the hub between Zion, Bryce, the Grand Canyon's North Rim, and the Wave.

pois.name: Bryce Canyon National Park
pois.blurb: An amphitheater of orange hoodoos at 8,000 feet. Cold at night, even in summer.

pois.name: Capitol Reef National Park
pois.blurb: A hundred-mile wrinkle in the earth, orchards in the desert, petroglyphs on the cliffs.

pois.name: Goblin Valley State Park
pois.blurb: A valley of mushroom-shaped hoodoos you can walk among, like a planet left unfinished.

pois.name: Moab
pois.blurb: Slickrock and the Colorado, mountain bikes and 4x4s, the base for two national parks.

pois.name: Arches National Park
pois.blurb: Over 2,000 stone arches, Delicate Arch alone on the rim against the La Sals.

pois.name: Canyonlands National Park
pois.blurb: Where the Green and the Colorado carve the earth into Islands in the Sky. No gas, no water.

pois.name: Salt Lake City
pois.blurb: The grid laid out from a temple, the Wasatch hard against the eastern edge.

pois.name: Lagoon Amusement Park (Farmington)
pois.blurb: Utah's own park since 1886: a wooden coaster from 1921 still rattling north of Salt Lake.

pois.name: Park City
pois.blurb: Old silver mines turned ski resort, Main Street steep with money and snow.

pois.name: Bonneville Salt Flats
pois.blurb: Thirty thousand acres of dead-flat salt where land-speed records are made. The horizon curves.

pois.name: Fallon / NAS Fallon
pois.blurb: Naval Air Station Fallon — TOPGUN moved here. Hornets tear the desert sky open low and loud.

pois.name: The Sphere, Las Vegas
pois.blurb: A 366-foot eyeball made of LEDs, blinking at the freeway. It is looking at you. It is always looking.

pois.name: Fremont Street, Las Vegas
pois.blurb: Old downtown under a canopy of a billion bulbs, a zipline screaming overhead, a cowboy made of neon.

pois.name: Seven Magic Mountains
pois.blurb: Stacks of fluorescent boulders rising out of the Jean dry lake, somebody's idea south of Vegas.

pois.name: Golden Gate Bridge
pois.blurb: International orange swallowed by fog. The towers come and go like a rumor.

pois.name: Racetrack Playa (Death Valley)
pois.blurb: The sailing stones. Rocks that move themselves across the mud and leave trails, and no one watching.

pois.name: Salvation Mountain
pois.blurb: A hand-painted adobe hill of love and scripture out by the Salton Sea, next to a town with no laws.

pois.name: Amargosa Opera House (Death Valley Junction)
pois.blurb: A lone opera house in the empty desert where a dancer painted herself an audience on the walls.

pois.name: Goldfield ghost town
pois.blurb: Once the biggest city in Nevada, now a few hundred souls, a haunted hotel, and a yard of welded art cars.

pois.name: The Integratron
pois.blurb: A white dome built from alien instructions for rejuvenation and time travel. Sound baths now. Sure.

pois.name: Madonna Inn, San Luis Obispo
pois.blurb: 110 rooms, no two alike, pink as a wound, a urinal that's a waterfall. You have to stay somewhere.

pois.name: Bigfoot country (Willow Creek)
pois.blurb: Self-proclaimed Bigfoot capital. A giant carved sasquatch by the road, and the trees lean in close.

pois.name: Area 51 back gate
pois.blurb: A cattle guard, a white truck on a hill, cameras on poles, and a sign that promises deadly force.

pois.name: koiNOya — Richmond
pois.blurb: A cluttered Edo-era relic shop in Richmond: naginata and ceremonial blades racked like umbrellas, each one carved with a card suit. Where Ace was born.

pois.name: AiSha Garage — Downtown Oakland
pois.blurb: A 1926 red-brick garage downtown, AiSHALLC hand-painted across the roofline, a kanji on the roll-up door, the skyline rising behind. Where Ace grew up.

pois.name: Petersen Automotive Museum, LA
pois.blurb: A red ribbon of steel wrapped around four floors of cars. She asks to idle out front a while.

pois.name: The Neon Museum, Las Vegas
pois.blurb: The Boneyard: dead casino signs laid out under the desert sky, still glowing if you squint.

pois.name: The Getty Center, LA
pois.blurb: Travertine and a tram up the hill — art, gardens, and the whole basin laid out below.

pois.name: Heard Museum, Phoenix
pois.blurb: The finest collection of Native American art in the Southwest, in a quiet Spanish-revival courtyard.

pois.name: Natural History Museum of Utah, SLC
pois.blurb: A copper-skinned ark built into the Wasatch foothills, full of dinosaurs and deep time.

pois.name: Pinball Hall of Fame, Las Vegas
pois.blurb: A warehouse of playable machines back to the 1950s. Bring quarters; leave the heat outside.

pois.name: Monterey
pois.blurb: Cannery Row, the kelp tanks, 17-Mile Drive. The cypress lean into the fog like they're listening.

pois.name: Long Beach
pois.blurb: The Queen Mary at anchor, the port cranes like grazing dinosaurs, the salvage yards inland.

pois.name: Livermore
pois.blurb: Wine country gone to office parks and self-storage. A row of roll-up doors keeps more secrets than any vault.

pois.name: San Jose
pois.blurb: The capital of Silicon Valley, flat and warm and endless.

pois.name: Berkeley
pois.blurb: The university, the hills, the smell of eucalyptus and protest.

pois.name: Sacramento
pois.blurb: The state capital under the delta breeze, old gold-rush bones downtown.

pois.name: Stockton
pois.blurb: A deep-water port ninety miles from the sea, asphalt shimmering in the valley heat.

pois.name: Santa Barbara
pois.blurb: Red-tile roofs, the Riviera of the West, the 101 running right along the surf.

pois.name: Ventura
pois.blurb: A pier, a point break, and the Channel Islands floating offshore.

pois.name: Oceanside
pois.blurb: Marine town, longboards, the smell of diesel and sunscreen.

pois.name: Riverside
pois.blurb: The Mission Inn and the orange groves that built it, inland and bright.

pois.name: Pasadena
pois.blurb: Craftsman bungalows, the Rose Bowl, the Colorado Street bridge over the arroyo.

pois.name: Palm Desert
pois.blurb: Golf and glass under the Santa Rosas, El Paseo for the snowbirds.

pois.name: Gilroy
pois.blurb: Garlic capital of the world; you smell it before the off-ramp.

pois.name: Napa
pois.blurb: Vines in tidy rows, tasting rooms, the wine train rattling north.

pois.name: Half Moon Bay
pois.blurb: Pumpkins, Mavericks' big surf, Highway 1 hugging the cliff edge.

pois.name: Redding
pois.blurb: Top of the valley under Mount Shasta, the Sundial Bridge over the Sacramento.

pois.name: Berlin–Ichthyosaur State Park
pois.blurb: A silver-rush ghost town nobody bothered to tear down — and behind it, under a shed, the bones of fifty-foot sea monsters that died here when Nevada was an ocean.
